title: The store as a React hook
objective: See how `create` turns the vanilla store into a hook, how `useStore` bridges it to React via useSyncExternalStore, and why no Provider is needed.

quiz.prompt: The module opens by tracing one `set(updater)` call through eight hand-offs. Which sequence matches the order the trace gives for the store side (steps 2 to 5)?

options.text: The updater runs against the current `state`; the replace-or-merge assignment runs; there is no store-level bail-out, so every listener is called and React's per-component comparison alone filters renders.
The updater runs against the current `state`; `Object.is` compares its return value with `state`; every listener is called with `(nextState, state)`; then the replace-or-merge assignment runs.
The updater runs against the current `state`; the replace-or-merge assignment runs; `Object.is` compares the merged result with `previousState`; every listener is called only if the two differ.
The updater runs against the current `state`; `Object.is` compares its return value with `state`; `previousState` is captured and the replace-or-merge assignment runs; then every listener is called.

quiz.prompt: Steps 6 and 7 describe what `useStore` hands to `React.useSyncExternalStore`. Which description matches the module?

options.text: `api.subscribe` unchanged, plus two memoized readers, `() => selector(api.getState())` and `() => selector(api.getInitialState())`; the selector runs inside the snapshot readers.
`api.subscribe`, `api.getState` and `api.getInitialState` unchanged; the hook returns the whole state object and `useStore` applies `selector` to that returned value afterward.
A wrapped subscribe that invokes React's callback only when `selector(api.getState())` has changed, plus `api.getState` as the single snapshot reader; the selector runs in the wrapper.
`api.subscribe`, a memoized `() => selector(api.getState())`, and `Object.is` passed as an `isEqual` argument; that third argument is how React decides whether the selected slice changed.

quiz.prompt: Step 4 of the trace is the replace-or-merge decision. For `set(nextState, replace)`, how does the module say that decision is made?

options.text: The type check wins outright: a non-object or `null` is always assigned wholesale; `replace` is consulted only for object values, where `true` assigns and `false` or omitted merges one level deep.
An explicit `replace` wins (`true` assigns wholesale, `false` merges); only when it is omitted does the fallback apply: a non-object or `null` is assigned, an object is merged one level deep.
`replace` defaults to `true` when the updater form `set(fn)` is used, since the function is expected to return the full state; the plain-object form defaults to a one-level merge.
An explicit `replace: true` assigns wholesale; otherwise the object is merged recursively, so a nested object you did not spread keeps its untouched keys instead of being replaced.

quiz.prompt: The module's warning box is precise about how zustand handles the 'zombie child' pitfall today versus in the past. Which account matches it?

options.text: It has always been structural: `src/react.ts` never uses React context, so a subscribed child cannot read a stale value from a provider; #550 and #2301 only changed where `useSyncExternalStore` is imported from, nothing else.

Until April 2022 it relied on React's experimental `useMutableSource`; #550 replaced that with the `use-sync-external-store` shim once React 18 shipped, and #2301 (Jan 2024) moved to `React.useSyncExternalStore` directly.

Until April 2022 it was hand-rolled with `useReducer` plus refs that re-checked state after subscribing; #550 deleted that in favor of the `use-sync-external-store` shim, and #2301 (Jan 2024) moved to `React.useSyncExternalStore` directly.

Until April 2022 it was hand-rolled with `useReducer` plus refs that re-checked state after subscribing; #550 deleted that and called `React.useSyncExternalStore` directly, and #2301 (Jan 2024) swapped in the `use-sync-external-store` shim for React 17.

quiz.prompt: `useBear` is both a hook and a handle: `useBear.getState()` works outside React. Which statement matches the module on what `create` staples onto the hook, and how?

options.text: `setState`, `getState`, `getInitialState` and `subscribe`, inherited through the prototype because the hook is built with `Object.create(api)` rather than having them copied on.
`getState`, `getInitialState` and `subscribe` only, the `ReadonlyStoreApi` subset; `setState` stays off the hook so that writes have to go through the store's actions.
`setState`, `getState`, `subscribe` and `destroy`, copied as own properties by `Object.assign(useBoundStore, api)` once the vanilla store has been built.
`setState`, `getState`, `getInitialState` and `subscribe`, copied as own properties by `Object.assign(useBoundStore, api)` once the vanilla store has been built.
